The tick rate is fixed when the engine is built, so the app carries both versions and loads the one you pick here. The change takes effect the next time you start the game. Both players in a match must be on the same rate.

The Windows client simulates at 60 Hz, and a 30 Hz client cannot stay in step with it, so cross-play has switched this device to 60 Hz. It takes effect the next time you start the game.\n\nThis doubles the simulation work per second. If the game runs slowly, turn cross-play off or set the rate back to 30 Hz under Graphics — but then you can only play against other Android players on 30 Hz.

Which graphics API the game uses. Takes effect the next time you launch the game, not live.

OpenGL ES (default): a native renderer written for this port. It is the default because it works on every device tested so far, including ones where Vulkan renders corrupted graphics. Start here; only change it if you have a reason to.

OpenGL ES + ANGLE: the same renderer, but routed through Google's ANGLE, which translates it to Vulkan, instead of your phone's own GLES driver. ANGLE is bundled inside this app, so it needs no minimum Android version and no system setting. Often faster once running, though a menu with many controls (Skirmish options) can stutter the first time it opens while ANGLE compiles what it needs; it does not stutter again until you leave and reopen that menu.

Vulkan: the original backend, through DXVK\u0027s Direct3D 8 to Vulkan translation. Faster than the others on phones whose driver handles it well, typically recent Snapdragon. But it depends entirely on that driver, and on some GPUs it produces magenta patches, distorted geometry or corrupted menus that no setting here can fix \u2014 PowerVR BXM and Samsung Xclipse have both been reported. If Vulkan looks wrong on your device, that is what the default is for.\n\nThe Custom Vulkan Driver and DXVK Config sections only appear when Vulkan is selected.
Saved. Takes effect next time you launch the game.

Custom Vulkan Driver (advanced, Adreno GPUs only)

Loads a Vulkan driver (a Mesa Turnip build) instead of your phone's built-in one, the same technique Winlator and AetherSX2 use. DXVK itself now only needs Vulkan 1.1, but some older Qualcomm Adreno stock drivers report even less (or have other bugs) — this Turnip build can let those phones run the game anyway. On a qualifying Adreno phone this is applied automatically — "Reset to Recommended" restores that automatic choice after you've imported something else.

This does NOT help Mali, PowerVR, or other non-Adreno GPUs — but those don't need it either: most Mali GPUs (Mali-G76, Mali-G57, and similar) already meet DXVK's Vulkan 1.1 requirement natively, no driver swap needed. This option is Adreno-only because Turnip only targets Adreno hardware, not because other GPUs are unsupported.

"Import Driver" lets you override the automatic choice with your own adrenotools-format driver .zip (for example from K11MCH1/AdrenoToolsDrivers or The412Banner/Banners-Turnip on GitHub). Takes effect next launch, not live.
No custom driver active — using your phone\'s built-in Vulkan driver.

Edits dxvk.conf directly, the same file the engine reads on startup — no rebuild needed, takes effect next launch. Useful settings if the game feels slow on your device:

d3d9.samplerAnisotropy = 2 (or 0 to disable) — lower than the default 16 to reduce GPU work on weaker hardware.
dxvk.hud = fps,drawcalls,submissions,pipelines — shows a small on-screen performance overlay.
dxvk.logLevel = none — keep this unless asked to change it; more verbose levels slow the game down.

One "key = value" per line. An invalid line is simply ignored by DXVK, so a typo won't break the game — worst case your change has no effect.
Saved. Takes effect next time you launch the game.

These turn on extra logging for bug reports — leave them all off for normal play, they can slow the game down or produce large logs. If someone reporting an issue asks you to turn one on, enable it, reproduce the problem, then use \"View Logs\" above to send the result.
Select a game folder first (above) to use these

Very detailed internal logging (UI, fonts, INI files) for chasing a specific hang or bug. Can grow to a huge log (50–100+ MB) over a long session — use \"Performance summary\" instead if you only need FPS numbers. (gx_trace.txt)

Draws the touch layer\'s own state over the game: current gesture, where your finger is, where the engine thinks the pointer is, and the camera scroll anchor. Turn this on to report control problems — a runaway map, a ghost building in the wrong place, an ability aiming somewhere you did not touch. (gx_touch_debug.txt)

Adds one short line per second showing where frame time goes (radar, audio, network, game logic, rendering). Safe to leave on for a whole play session — turn this on for FPS/slowdown reports. (gx_perf.txt)

Measures how long the GPU spends on each frame and adds it to the performance summary, to tell whether the GPU or the CPU is the limit. OpenGL ES only. Some Mali drivers crash with it, so leave it off unless you are asked for it. (gx_gles_gputimer.txt)

Records what the sound system is doing: music and speech buffer levels, movie audio, and every source that starts or stops. Turn this on if you are asked for an audio log after reporting missing, stuttering or silent sound. (gx_audio_trace.txt)

Records every request the game makes to the GeneralsOnline servers, with the reply it got. Turn this on if sign-in, the lobby or matchmaking fails from inside the game. The launcher\'s own requests are always recorded; this adds the game\'s. It also turns on the cross-play desync diagnostics: the simulation checksums that are compared each interval, and, in a replay, the checksum of every single object. The checksum of every single object is written only during a Replay check, so ordinary games are not slowed down. (gx_net_trace.txt)

Shows FPS, draw calls, submissions, and pipeline count directly on screen and in the log. Turn this on for GPU performance reports. (dxvk_hud.txt)

1. "Select Game Folder" opens a folder browser on your phone's storage. Navigate to wherever you copied your own Command & Conquer Generals Zero Hour install (the folder containing INIZH.big, Data\, ZH_Generals\, etc.) and tap "Use This Folder".

2. If browsing looks empty, Android is asking for the "All files access" permission first — grant it in the screen that opens (this is a normal Android permission, no root involved).

3. "View Logs" shows the engine log and, if the game crashed, a native crash log — no computer or adb needed. Use the Share button there to send the log to yourself.

4. "Launch Game" starts the game with the folder you picked.

Tap Sign In. The first tap may ask to exempt this app from battery optimization -- allow it, then come back and tap Sign In again. A browser then opens to playgenerals.online, already carrying a one-time code for this device. Pick Steam, Discord, or GameReplays there, then just come back to this app; it finishes on its own.

Reports the Windows client\'s EXE checksum so its games will accept you. That checksum is not anti-cheat — it is what keeps two machines that would compute the match differently from playing it together, so this can desync the game for everyone in the lobby. Turn it on for a PC you own, and only after copying that PC\'s INI data into this game folder so the two really do match.

Nothing is pushed off the screen: each part grows only as far as it fits, so the control bar gets taller rather than wider on a wide phone, and the battlefield above it gets shorter. Two fingers = scroll the map, pinch = zoom. Takes effect the next time the game starts. The game\'s own \"Alternate mouse setup\" option still decides what the left and right buttons do. Online matches keep every player in step, so a slow phone slows everyone. If your device stays at 45 FPS or below for 30 seconds, or freezes for 20 seconds, it leaves the match automatically; after repeated cases it is limited to 4-player lobbies until a match runs smoothly. Lowering the graphics settings or using a phone cooler helps.
Choose internal render resolution. The game output is always stretched to fill the full screen.

Lower resolutions (e.g. 720p or 540p) noticeably improve FPS and reduce thermal throttling, and the picture always fills the screen. A custom size keeps at least the 4:3 shape and 600 lines the game\'s menus need.

Short lessons for new commanders. Tap a topic to open it.

Build your supply building next to a supply pile and keep your gatherers working: money wins games. USA and China need power, so build power plants early; GLA does not. Scout with a cheap unit to see what the enemy is building, then counter it. Select a group and press Ctrl + a number to save it, then that number to call it back. Keep every factory producing.

Strong air force (Raptor, Comanche, Aurora) and well-armored, expensive units. Rangers clear garrisoned buildings with flash-bangs. Patriot batteries and Avengers protect against aircraft. Weak against many cheap units early on: protect your Chinooks and expand carefully.

Heavy armor (Battlemaster, Overlord) and area damage (Dragon tanks, Inferno and Nuke Cannons). Hackers make money and Gattling units shred infantry and aircraft. Infantry and Battlemasters fight better in groups (Horde bonus). Weak against air and long-range artillery: build Gattling Cannons and keep your army together.

Fast, cheap and hidden. No power needed. Technicals and Quad Cannons strike early; Scorpions and Marauders upgrade by salvaging wrecks. Tunnel Networks move your army across the map. Weak in open fights against heavy armor: hit and run, raid supplies and choose where to fight.

1. Spend your money: a large bank is lost time. 2. Keep building gatherers until every supply pile is worked. 3. Scout early and again later. 4. Do not attack into defenses: flank them or out-range them. 5. Pull back damaged units; veterans are worth saving. 6. Use team keys and your hotkeys to give orders fast.

- Pro Rules are community-agreed laws for clean and balanced play. Breaking them can get you banned!
- Rules vary by map or match type. If unsure, ask the HOST before starting.
## General Pro Rules (especially Twilight Flame 3v3 $50k):
 - 🚫 No Superweapons at all (Particle Cannon, Nuclear Missile, SCUD Storm).
 - 🚫 No Auroras & Alpha Auroras.
 - 🚫 No Demo Bikes.
 - 🚫 No Nuke MiG Upgrade.
 - 🚫 No Stealth Comanche.
 - 🚫 No Carpet Bomb for USA Air Force before reaching ⭐⭐⭐.
 - 🛑 Max 2 of each defense type at your entrance or oil (Patriots, Gattling Cannons, Stinger Sites, EMP).
 - ✅ Unlimited Tunnels are allowed.

- Matches with no restrictions on army abilities. Everything is allowed ✅
## Exception: 🚫 Intentional bug abuse is strictly forbidden.
- 🔍 Definition of a bug: an error, flaw, or fault in the game that causes an incorrect or unintended result.
- Examples: using cars to destroy on certain maps, building in enemy territory to block units or remove supply crates, or any unnatural game behavior.
- 🚨 Using any bug leads to an immediate ban without discussion!
- Often used in $10,000 games.
These are the basic rules of Generals Zero Hour. Respect the rules and play like a pro! 💪😎

Two fingers always move the camera: drag to pan, pinch to zoom, twist to turn. With Move selected, one finger pans too. A fast swipe keeps gliding (turn it off in Settings). The house in the menu brings the camera back to the start.

Raise and Lower build hills and valleys, Smooth softens them, Height sets an exact level. Hold your finger still or drag; the panel at the bottom sets the brush size, the soft edge and the strength. Undo takes back a whole stroke.

Pick a category and an object in the panel (or search for it), then tap the map. Drag while placing to turn it. Choose its owner with Owner. With Select you move, turn or delete what is already there.

Tap to place a waypoint; drag from one to another to link them into a path. Name a waypoint Player_1_Start … Player_8_Start to make it a player\'s start position (the chips in the panel do it in one tap); InitialCameraPosition is where the game camera begins. A new map starts with Player 1 and 2; keep the starts inside the line around the map, or the game opens on a black screen.
Choose Areas, tap the corners of a region and tap the first corner again to close it. Select an area to rename it. Scripts use areas to ask things like “has a unit entered this place?”.

Scripts (top bar or tool bar) open players, teams and scripts. A script says: IF these conditions are true, THEN do these actions (OTHERWISE others). Add players and teams first, then scripts in folders. Nothing reaches the map until you press OK, and one Undo takes the whole change back.

Save writes your own map back to its file (the first time it asks: overwrite, or save a copy); the button next to it, Save as, makes a copy under a new name. Maps go to your Maps folder in the PC format, so they appear in the game\'s map list and play on PC too. A map from the game\'s archives is always saved as a copy. Before saving, the start positions are checked.
